_meta.title: DemoBlaze: add to cart, review cart total, place an order
_meta.disclaimer: Every entity, identity, product, card number, address and identifier in this file is synthetic and invented for QAIA fixture/test purposes only. No real shopper, no real payment instrument, no real catalog record and no personal data of any kind is present. The card values are deliberately non-numeric so they cannot be mistaken for, or accidentally submitted as, a real PAN. Prices and cart totals are fixture arithmetic, not a price list of any real storefront.

assumptions.about: product identity vs. the real target catalog
assumptions.text: dataset-generate step 6 forbids reusing a real product/company name, but the system under test (DemoBlaze) serves a real catalog and AC1/AC4 are only exercisable against a real catalog product id. This fixture resolves the conflict in favour of step 6: every product here carries a synthetic title and `externalCatalogId: null`. Any test that must hit the live target has to resolve a catalog id at runtime (e.g. from the first tile on the landing page) and must NOT read one from this file. This is a fixture convention, not a claim about the target's catalog.

The two prices used by the AC4-C2 accumulation case are taken verbatim from the already-validated test book (testbooks/cart-checkout.feature line 45: 'fetched prices of $360 and $790'), not invented here. They are attached to synthetic product titles per ASM-1. Numeric prices are carried over as-is; only names are synthesised.

assumptions.about: the exact whitespace used for AC7-C3
assumptions.text: 03-design AC7-C3 says 'a whitespace-only string (e.g. a single space)'. The source is silent on tab / NBSP / multiple spaces. This fixture uses exactly one U+0020 in OF-004 and does not assert anything about other whitespace forms.

03-design section 3b confirms the target performs no format/Luhn/expiry validation on the card field; oracle-generate was deliberately not invoked. Card values here are therefore intentionally non-numeric, obviously-synthetic strings ('SYNTHETIC-CARD-nnnn'). They are NOT test PANs and must never be treated as card-format fixtures.

cases.description: Cart holding a single non-integer-priced item (1150.5): does the displayed total truncate?

expectedResult.rule: 01-extraction 'What was NOT found' states it is unknown whether any catalogue product ever carries a non-integer price, which is exactly what turns AC4's parseInt from theoretical to a confirmed rounding defect. This case exposes the fork rather than resolving it.
interpretations: Interpretation A — parseInt truncation is intended display behaviour: the UI shows 1150 while the true cart value is 1150.5 (a 0.5 under-charge shown to the shopper).
Interpretation B — truncation is a defect: the UI is expected to show 1150.5 (or a rounded 1151) and the parseInt is a bug to raise.

cases.description: Deleting one row of a three-item cart: request fires with no confirmation, total recomputes without that row.

expectedResult.rule: POST /deleteitem fires immediately for CI-005, no confirm prompt, reload, total becomes 1180 (AC5)

cases.description: Opening 'Place Order' shows all six fields plus the Total label.

expectedResult.rule: Name, Country, City, Credit card, Month, Year and the Total label are all present (AC6)

cases.description: The four never-read fields (Country, City, Month, Year), empty in one form and garbage in the other, change nothing.

expectedResult.rule: submission is never blocked by these four fields and none of their values appears in the confirmation dialog (AC6, source-confirmed: purchaseOrder() never reads them)

cases.description: Name empty, Credit card non-empty.

cases.description: Name non-empty, Credit card empty (symmetric to C-015).

expectedResult.rule: alert 'Please fill out Name and Creditcard.'; no order id; modal stays open (AC7)

cases.description: Credit card is exactly one space — boundary of the == "" check, no .trim() in source.

expectedResult.rule: no 'Please fill out Name and Creditcard.' alert; the purchase proceeds to the confirmation dialog (AC7-C3)

cases.description: Valid purchase from a two-item cart: confirmation dialog shows Id, Amount, verbatim card, Name, date.

expectedResult.rule: dialog contains a generated Id, Amount 1150 USD, Card Number 'SYNTHETIC-CARD-0001' verbatim, Name 'Ava Sample-01', current date; POST /deletecart fired (AC8)

cases.description: The dialog's Amount equals the total displayed on the cart page before purchasing.

expectedResult.rule: Amount = 1150, i.e. the page-load-time total; single-session scope only (AC8-C2 / Q2)

cases.description: A guest with no session token completes the identical purchase flow.

expectedResult.rule: Q3 in the US is unresolved: no login gate was found in the captured source, either way. Observed behaviour is asserted by the test book scenario; whether it is CORRECT is the fork below and is left for human arbitration.
interpretations: Interpretation A — guest checkout is intended policy: the dialog appears identically for SHOP-001 and this case passes as written.
Interpretation B — purchasing should require login: the absence of a gate is a defect, and this exact data would be the reproduction case for it.

cases.description: Placing an order against an empty cart still succeeds with Amount 0.

expectedResult.rule: order id generated, dialog Amount = 0 USD, no emptiness guard blocks it (AC8-C4, S0->S3)

cases.description: Confirming the success dialog navigates to index.html.

expectedResult.rule: OK on the dialog -> navigation to index.html (AC9)
